- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for risk reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.  
- If 3+ consecutive days of low sentiment (≤0.3) or high volatility, model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days) — apply downward correction of 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
